questions.question: Run B must start from master plus exactly one variant commit. This branch already carries the last session's decision-log commit, and this session will add its own log. Where do the logs go?

options.label: Logs to master first (Recommended)
options.description: Small separate PR with both decision logs, merged before run B. The variant branch is then rebased to one commit that touches only ship/SKILL.md, so run B's base is clean and its recorded commit pair is accurate.

options.label: Fold into variant commit
options.description: Squash everything into one commit on the variant branch. It's simpler, but the logs never reach master unless they're cherry-picked later, and the variant commit touches sdd/decisions/ too.

options.label: Leave as two commits
options.description: Keep c97968c3d below the variant commit. Run B would then start from master + 2 commits, a small departure from RFC-0020's stated start condition.

questions.question: P2 needs the build session to stop at PR open and a fresh session to take over. How should the second session start?

options.label: /clear, then /ship resume <PR> (Recommended)
options.description: Same terminal and worktree. /clear gives a new transcript and session ID. The handoff lives in the worktree's tmp/ship-handoff-<PR>.md (gitignored, copied into token-kit runs/ for the record). The second prompt is fixed in advance like the first.

options.label: New terminal, /ship resume <PR>
options.description: A fully separate claude process in the same worktree. Same effect on context as /clear, just more manual steps.

options.label: Handoff committed to the trace
options.description: The handoff goes into the BK-418/BUG-280 trace instead of tmp/, so it's durable on the PR. It adds trace content reviewers read, which is a small priming risk.

questions.question: P4: how long may a background wait run before the session reports and stops waiting? Run A's foreground gate had a median of 194 s, the tool limit is 600 s, and the stall was 37 min.

options.label: 15 min (Recommended)
options.description: About 4.6× the median gate and 1.5× the tool limit. It would have cut run A's 37-min stall to 15.

options.label: 10 min
options.description: Tighter. It risks cutting off a legitimately slow full suite under load.

options.label: 30 min
options.description: Loose. It barely changes run A's 37-min case.

questions.question: How much review should the variant get before run B? A wrong variant wastes a ~$50–140 run, and every review pass spends tokens.

options.label: Draft PR, your review only (Recommended)
options.description: Open it as a draft PR marked 'do not merge' so the diff has a review surface, and skip /rvw-pr. You read it and I fix what you flag. It's the cheapest option, and what matters is whether it says what RFC-0020 says, which you know best.

options.label: Draft PR + one /rvw-pr pass
options.description: One unprimed reviewer checks the diff against RFC-0020 § Proposal. Moderate cost, and it catches mechanism text that is inert or contradicts the Stop rule.

options.label: Branch only, no PR
options.description: Push the branch, no PR. That's minimal, but there's no record of the variant's review.
